title: The Current of the Upper Fly River
premise: Quentin Underhill, a desert ranger with a reputation for finding people who don't want to be found, is hired to track a thief who stole a surveyor's journal from the Amberdale Trust. The trail leads not across her familiar dunes but up the Upper Fly River, where an expedition led by the Trust's heir has gone silent. As Quentin climbs toward the river's forbidden source, she discovers the thief stole the journal to hide evidence that the source sits on sacred ground the Trust intends to dam — and that the missing expedition's leader is the woman Quentin once loved and abandoned for duty. When the monsoon breaks early, Quentin must choose between delivering the truth to the courts or destroying it to protect the river and the people who guard it; she chooses the river, burning the journal but testifying from memory, losing her ranger's commission and gaining a life at the water's edge.
about_author: Isandro Amberdale is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years mapping remote tributaries before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels in which landscapes behave like characters with long memories.

chapters.title: Salt and Sign
chapters.summary: Quentin Underhill tracks a thief named Wren Calloway across the Redglass Flats, reading broken scrub and buried footprints like scripture. She recovers nothing but a torn map corner bearing the Fly River's headwaters. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: competence masking loneliness — she is the best tracker alive and no one waits for her at home.

chapters.title: The Trust's Letter
chapters.summary: In the town of Marrow Bend, Quentin is summoned by Aldous Vane of the Amberdale Trust: the thief stole a surveyor's journal, and an expedition led by Dr. Imogen Hale went silent upstream three weeks ago. He offers Quentin double her fee to retrieve both. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: cold dread — Imogen's name lands like a stone in still water.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: Quentin hires a flatboat pilot, old Sefu Marr, who warns that the Upper Fly forgives nothing and forgets less. The first night aboard, she reads the stolen map fragment and recognizes Imogen's handwriting on its margin notes. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: grief resurfacing — duty took her from Imogen seven years ago, and the river is handing the debt back.

chapters.title: Wren in the Reeds
chapters.summary: Quentin ambushes Wren Calloway at a fueling dock; instead of fighting, Wren claims the journal proves the Trust plans to dam the sacred source and that the expedition was never meant to come back. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: defiant fear — she trusts the tracker exactly as far as the river is wide.

chapters.title: First Rapids
chapters.summary: Sefu pilots them through the Serrated Reach while a Trust patrol boat shadows them. Quentin realizes Vane sent a second team upstream ahead of her — one that doesn't answer radios either. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: suspicion hardening into resolve; the employer is becoming the enemy.

chapters.title: The Drowned Village
chapters.summary: They pass a village half-submerged by an earlier Trust 'survey flood.' An elder, Maren Oduya, tells them the river has a keeper at its source and that strangers who take from it are kept by it. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: guilt and awe — Wren sees what her theft set in motion.

chapters.title: Radio Silence
chapters.summary: At an abandoned expedition camp, Quentin finds Imogen's radio smashed deliberately, not storm-damaged, and a message scratched into a supply crate: DON'T TRUST VANE. TURN BACK. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: terror braided with hope — Imogen is alive and thinking of her.

chapters.title: The Second Team
chapters.summary: The Trust patrol catches up; its leader, Captain Rook, orders Quentin to surrender Wren and return downstream. Quentin stalls, then scuttles the patrol's fuel cache under cover of a squall. POV: Rook. Emotional beat: professional contempt curdling into obsession — Rook wants the source found at any cost.

chapters.title: Monsoon Signs
chapters.summary: Sefu reads the sky and gives them four days before landfall. The trio abandons the boat and goes overland through leech-thick jungle toward the gorge. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: humility — the desert ranger must learn the river's grammar from Wren and Sefu.

chapters.title: Confession at the Fire
chapters.summary: Wren admits she was once the Trust's own surveyor and forged nothing: the journal's dam schematics are real. Quentin admits she abandoned Imogen because Vane threatened her commission. POV: alternating close-third. Emotional beat: two liars trading truths by firelight, loyalty beginning to outweigh fear.

chapters.title: The Gorge of Names
chapters.summary: They climb the gorge where every ledge bears carved names of the river's dead keepers. A rope bridge fails; Sefu falls and survives, barely, but his maps are lost. POV: Sefu. Emotional beat: sacrifice without regret — the old pilot says the river only borrows.

chapters.title: Keepers
chapters.summary: Source-keepers find them and march them blindfolded to a hidden valley where the surviving expedition lives — including Imogen, who has chosen exile over letting Vane's second team reach the spring. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: guarded fury meeting old love; seven years of silence in one look.

chapters.title: The Forbidden Source
chapters.summary: Imogen shows Quentin the spring: a cathedral of water rising from limestone, ringed by terraces the keepers have tended for centuries. The dam would drown it all. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: conversion — she stops being hired help and becomes a believer.

chapters.title: Rook Arrives
chapters.summary: Rook's team breaches the valley with monsoon flooding behind them. In the chaos, Rook seizes the journal from Wren's pack and takes Imogen hostage as his guide to the spring. POV: Rook. Emotional beat: triumph curdling — even he can hear the river rising.

chapters.title: Landfall
chapters.summary: The monsoon hits in full. The gorge floods, stranding everyone above it together. Rook, cut off from extraction, bargains: the journal for safe passage down. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: clarity under pressure — the storm strips away every easy option.

chapters.title: The Keeper's Price
chapters.summary: Maren Oduya arrives with the keepers' council. Their law: those who take from the source are kept by it. Rook refuses to give back the journal; the council will not let anyone leave with it. Standoff in the rain. POV: Wren. Emotional beat: Wren choosing sides at last — she stands with the keepers.

chapters.title: Climax: The Rising Water
chapters.summary: Flash flood funnels into the valley. Quentin goes after Rook alone, fights him on the drowning terraces, and recovers the journal as the spring itself seems to swallow the intruders' camp. Rook is swept into a side channel and lost. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: the fight of her life, won not by strength but by knowing how water moves.

chapters.title: Kept by the River
chapters.summary: In the aftermath, the council rules: the journal stays, the strangers may go, but Quentin must choose — leave and testify against the Trust from memory, or stay and be kept. Imogen asks her, plainly, to stay. POV: Imogen. Emotional beat: love making its demand without apology.

chapters.title: The Long Way Down
chapters.summary: Quentin descends the flooded river with Sefu and Wren, memorizing every page of the journal before surrendering it to the keepers. She drafts her testimony in her head against the sound of the current. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: quiet resolve — memory as an act of loyalty to truth.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: In Marrow Bend, Quentin testifies before the water commission, reciting the dam schematics and the drowned village from memory. Vane's charter is suspended pending inquiry; he threatens her with ruin and finds she no longer owns anything worth ruining. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: liberation through loss — the commission stripped, the conscience clear.

chapters.title: What Duty Owes Love
chapters.summary: Quentin returns to the upper river, this time openly, carrying gifts and her ranger's badge surrendered to Vane's office. The keepers grant her a place at the valley's edge; Imogen meets her at the terraces. POV: both, braided. Emotional beat: homecoming — duty finally pointed in the right direction.

chapters.title: The Current Remembers
chapters.summary: A year later, Quentin runs a small rescue post at the gorge mouth with Sefu and Wren, pulling stranded travelers from the river that forgives nothing. On the anniversary of the flood, she carves no name into the gorge walls — the river already keeps hers. POV: Quentin. Emotional beat: peace earned, not given; the wilderness forgets less, but it also holds on.
